questions.question:
**Select the antonym of the given word.**

LAMENT
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Rejoice. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The most appropriate antonym of the given word** 'Lament' **is** 'Rejoice'. **
 
• Let's look at the meaning and examples of the given words: 
 
 
• 
 
 
 

 **Lament**
 to express sadness and feeling sorry about something
 *Ex. The poem opens by **lamenting **(over) the death of a young man.*
 
 

 **Rejoice**
 to feel or show great happiness about something
 *Ex. Everyone **rejoiced **at the news of his safe return.*
 
 

 **Regret**
 a feeling of sadness about something sad or wrong or about a mistake that you have made, and a wish that it could have been different and better
 *Ex. The manager expressed deep **regret **at the number of staff reductions.*
 
 

 **Grieve**
 to feel or express great sadness, especially when someone dies
 *Ex. He is still **grieving **over his wife.*
 
 

 **Mourn**
 to feel or express great sadness, especially because of someone's death
 *Ex.They **mourned **the passing of an older, simpler way of life. *
 
 
 
 
 
 

Therefore, by reading the above explanation we find that the correct answer is *'Rejoice'. *

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error from the given options.**

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** is normal. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect. 
 
• The erroneous Part **'in normal'** should be **'is normally'. **
 
• When modifying an entire sentence, adverbs can be placed in four positions:
 
 
• **at the beginning;** **at the end;** **after the verb "to be" and "all auxiliary verbs": **can, may, will, must, shall, and have, when have is used as an auxiliary (for example in I have been in Spain twice); before all the other verbs.
 
• Example of adverb **after the auxiliary verb:** 
 
 
• *The summer is **usually **hot and humid.*
 
 
 
 
 
• Therefore, cannot be used between the helping verb and **the main verb. **
 
• Hence, the correct answer is** Option 4. **

 ​

**Correct Sentence:__** *The jute plant **is normally** harvested when it is at flowering stage. *

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.**

The ______ of the minister’s statement cannot be verified by people who have no access to official records.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'validity'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word** 'Validity' **means **'the quality of being based on truth or reason, or of being able to be accepted'. **(सत्य या कारण पर आधारित होने या स्वीकार किए जाने में सक्षम होने का गुण)** **

 
 
• *Example: This research seems to give some **validity **to the theory that the drug might cause cancer.*
 
 
 
• The given sentence is talking about the** truthfulness **of the minister's statement. And the most appropriate word for that is** 'Validity'. (**दिया गया वाक्य मंत्री के बयान की सत्यता की बात कर रहा है। और उसके लिए सबसे उपयुक्त शब्द है '**validity**')
 
• It is so because only the truthfulness of the minister's statement can be verified. (ऐसा इसलिए है क्योंकि केवल मंत्री के बयान की सत्यता की पुष्टि की जा सकती है)
 
• **Option 2** and **4** can be eliminated as they do not fit in the context of the sentence. (विकल्प 2 और 4 को समाप्त किया जा सकता है क्योंकि वे वाक्य के संदर्भ में फिट नहीं होते हैं)
 
• **Option 3** cannot be the correct answer.
 
• It is so because the statement **'**The **approval** of the minister's statement cannot be verified by people who have no access to official records'** **does not make sense.

questions.question:

This seems to be a ______ rifle.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'soldier's'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given question we use **apostrophe s (’s),** also called possessive ’s, as **a determiner **to show that something** belongs to someone or something.**

 
 
• *Example: **Britain’s **coastline is very beautiful. *
 
 
 
• Here, the rifle belongs to that particular soldier. Hence, shows the possession. 
 
• All other options form grammatically incorrect statement because there is either no possessive used or its position is incorrect. And, *soldier *cannot be used as an adjective for the noun *rifle*

 ​

**Correct Sentence:** *This seems to be a **soldier's** rifle. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• We can also use **possessive **in complex **noun phrases** (underlined). 

 
 
• *Example: Greg is her youngest **daughter’s** husband.*
 
 
 
• We can use **two possessive ’s **constructions in the same noun phrase. 
 
 
• *Example: We went to Jake’s **father’s** funeral.*
 
 
 
• We **"use ’s"** after a singular noun and** ’ **after **a plural noun.**
 
• Let's see the comparison: 
 
 
• 
 
 
 

 **singular noun + ’s**
 **plural noun + ’**
 
 

 
 
*The girl’s bedroom*

 
(The bedroom belongs to one girl.)

 
 
 
*The girls’ bedroom.*

 
(The bedroom belongs to more than one girl.)
